He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]] and was selected with the seventh overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Sacramento Kings]]. McLemore played for five teams in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) across a nine-year career. McLemore spent four seasons with the Kings before signing with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in 2017. He was traded back to the Kings in 2018 and then signed with the [[Houston Rockets]] in 2019. McLemore joined the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in 2021 and spent his final NBA stint with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] during the 2021–22 season. McLemore played overseas in [[China]], [[Greece]], [[Spain]] and [[Turkey]] from 2023 to 2025. In 2025, McLemore was sentenced to eight years' imprisonment after he was found guilty of raping a woman in Oregon. ==High school career== McLemore played [[basketball#High school basketball|high school basketball]] at Wellston High School in [[St. Louis|St. Louis, Missouri]] for three years before his school was shut down in 2010. He then attended both [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] in [[Mouth of Wilson, Virginia]] and [[Christian Life Center Academy (Humble, Texas)|Christian Life Center]] in [[Humble, Texas]] during his senior year of high school. Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], McLemore was listed as the No. 9 shooting guard and the No. 34 player in the nation in 2011.{{cite news|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Ben-McLemore-108908|title=Ben McLemore Recruiting Profile|work=Rivals.com|access-date=October 4, 2015}} ==College career== After committing to Kansas, McLemore was deemed ineligible to play by the NCAA because he attended multiple high schools, resulting in his transcripts being "a little fuzzy".{{cite web|last=Keeley |first=Sean |url=https://www.sbnation.com/ncaa-basketball/2011/10/14/2491002/kansas-freshmen-ben-mclemore-jamari-traylor-ineligible |title=Kansas Declares Freshmen Ben McLemore, Jamari Traylor Ineligible |publisher=SBNation.com |date=October 14, 2011 |access-date=March 8, 2013}} He was allowed to practice with the team and take part in team activities starting in the second semester of the school year.{{cite web|last=Bedore |first=Gary |url=http://www2.ljworld.com/news/2011/oct/14/ku-freshmen-ben-mclemore-jamari-traylor-ineligible/ |title=KU freshmen Ben McLemore, Jamari Traylor ineligible for 2011-12 season / LJWorld.com |publisher=.ljworld.com |access-date=March 8, 2013}} At the beginning of his college career, McLemore was considered to be either a late first-round or early second-round prospect. However, during his first season as a redshirt freshman, McLemore averaged 15.9 [[Point (basketball)|points]], 5.2 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] and 2.0 [[Assist (basketball)|assists]], with 49.5% [[Field goal percentage|shooting from the field]] and 87% shooting from the [[Foul shot|foul line]],{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/players/1904504/ben-mclemore/ |title=Ben McLemore, Kansas, NCAA Basketball |access-date=March 8, 2013|website=CBSSports.com|url-status=dead}} and was named a finalist for the [[John R. Wooden Award]].{{cite news|url=http://throughthephog.com/2013/03/09/withey-mclemore-named-to-wooden-finalist-list/|title=Withey, McLemore Named to Wooden Finalist List|work=ThroughThePhog.com|date=March 9, 2013|access-date=October 4, 2015|archive-date=June 8, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130608154812/http://throughthephog.com/2013/03/09/withey-mclemore-named-to-wooden-finalist-list/|url-status=dead}} After declaring for the [[2013 NBA draft]], allegations arose that NBA agent Rodney Blackstock had given thousands of dollars in impermissible benefits to McLemore's AAU coach, Darius Cobb, in exchange for Cobb steering McLemore toward certain financial advisers and NBA agents.{{cite news |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2013/06/26/kansas-jayhawks-ben-mclemore-rodney-blackstock-nba-draft/2461551/ |title=Why Ben McLemore chose Rodney Blackstock as his agent |newspaper=USA Today |date=June 28, 2013 |first=Nicole |last=Auerbach}} Lending credence to Cobb's allegations, McLemore had Blackstock on his guest pass list for at least three Kansas home games that season, and subsequently signed Blackstock as his NBA agent. This set of facts caused the launch of an NCAA investigation to determine whether or not Kansas would have to vacate the basketball games in which McLemore played. ==Professional career== ===Sacramento Kings (2013–2017)=== [[File:Ben McLemore - 2013 Green Room invites (9156599280).jpg|upright|thumb|McLemore during the 2013 NBA draft]] McLemore was selected with the seventh overall pick by the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the [[2013 NBA draft]].{{cite news |url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-select-ben-mclemore-first-round |title=KINGS SELECT BEN MCLEMORE IN FIRST ROUND |work=NBA.com |date=June 27, 2013 |access-date=November 21, 2013}} On July 13, 2013, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Kings and joined them for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]].{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-2013-first-round-pick-ben-mclemore|title=Kings Sign 2013 First-Round Pick Ben McLemore|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2013|access-date=October 4, 2015}} He was named the Western Conference Rookie of the Month for November 2013.{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-ben-mclemore-named-western-conference-rookie-month-november|title=Kings Ben McLemore named Western Conference Rookie of the Month for November|work=NBA.com|date=December 3, 2013|access-date=October 4, 2015}} In February 2014, McLemore was selected to participate in the 2014 Sprite Slam Dunk contest.{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/ben-mclemore-selected-2014-sprite-slam-dunk-contest|title=Ben McLemore Selected to 2014 Sprite Slam Dunk Contest|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2014|access-date=October 4, 2015}} In the Kings' final game of the regular season on April 16, McLemore scored a season-high 31 points in a loss to the Phoenix Suns.{{cite news|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/mclembe01/gamelog/2014/|title=Ben McLemore 2013-14 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=October 4, 2015}} In his rookie season, he played all 82 games (55 starts), averaging 8.8 points, 2.9 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 26.7 minutes per game. In July 2014, McLemore re-joined the Kings for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]] where he helped them win the Summer League championship while averaging 12.6 points in seven games. On October 19, 2014, the Kings exercised their third-year team option on McLemore's rookie-scale contract, extending the contract through the 2015–16 season.{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-pick-option-guard-ben-mclemore|title=Kings Pick Up Option on Guard Ben McLemore|work=NBA.com|date=October 19, 2014|access-date=October 19, 2014}} On March 11, 2015, he scored a season-high 27 points in a win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite news|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/mclembe01/gamelog/2015/|title=Ben McLemore 2014-15 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=October 4, 2015}} He started in all 82 regular season games for the Kings in 2014–15 while averaging 12.1 points, 2.9 rebounds and 1.7 assists in 32.6 minutes per game. On October 3, 2015, the Kings exercised their fourth-year team option on McLemore's rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the 2016–17 season.{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/blog/kings-pick-option-ben-mclemore|title=Kings Pick Up Option on Ben McLemore|work=NBA.com|date=October 3, 2015|access-date=October 4, 2015}} On December 5, he had a season-best game with 19 points and 9 rebounds in a loss to the Houston Rockets.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/mclembe01/gamelog/2016/ Ben McLemore 2015-16 Game Log] On January 28, 2016, he scored a season-high 26 points in a loss to the New Orleans Pelicans.[http://www.nba.com/kings/blog/kings-fall-nop-comeback Kings Unable To Complete Comeback] On February 1, McLemore missed his first game of his career due to a sprained right wrist, snapping his consecutive games streak at 211, which was the second-longest in the NBA behind [[Tristan Thompson]] (335).[http://www.nba.com/games/20160201/MILSAC/gameinfo.html Gay scores 32 to lead Kings over Bucks, 111-104] He later missed 10 games in March with a finger-tip injury.[http://www.nba.com/games/20160327/DALSAC/gameinfo.html Cauley-Stein scores 21 points, Kings beat Mavs 133-111] On February 10, 2017, McLemore had a season-high 22 points, helped by a career-best six three-pointers, in a 108–107 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900211|title=Kings rally from 22 down to beat Hawks 108-107|work=ESPN.com|date=February 10, 2017|access-date=February 11, 2017}} On March 29, 2017, he tied a season high with 22 points in a 112–82 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 12, 2025 |date=November 4, 2018}} On July 4, 2015, Wellston Avenue, the street on which McLemore grew up, was renamed Ben McLemore III Place in his honor.{{cite web |last=Choat |first=Brad |date=July 4, 2015 |title=NBA Player Comes Home to Wellston |url=http://stlouis.cbslocal.com/2015/07/04/nba-player-comes-home-to-wellston/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170818093108/http://stlouis.cbslocal.com/2015/07/04/nba-player-comes-home-to-wellston/ |archive-date=August 18, 2017 |access-date=November 7, 2017 |work=cbslocal.com}} McLemore was previously married.{{cite web |title=Ex-NBA player Ben McLemore found guilty of rape by Oregon jury.|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/ex-nba-player-ben-mclemore-found-guilty-of-rape-by-oregon-jury/ |website=CBS News |access-date=July 4, 2025 |date=July 3, 2025}} In March 2017, McLemore's first child, Teagan, was born.{{cite web |last=Ham |first=James |date=March 22, 2017 |title=Ben McLemore returns after birth of his daughter: 'Dream come true' |url=http://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/kings/ben-mclemore-returns-after-birth-his-daughter-dream-come-true |access-date=November 7, 2017 |work=nbcsports.com}} In March 2024, McLemore was involved in a drunken driving incident in [[Lugo]], Spain.{{Cite web|title=And-Ones: Lamb, Thomas, McLemore, Biggest Buyers|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/03/and-ones-lamb-thomas-mclemore-biggest-buyers.html|access-date=March 15, 2024|website=hoopsrumors.com|date=March 10, 2024 |language=en}} ===Rape conviction=== On April 9, 2024, McLemore was arrested by [[Clackamas County]] Sheriff's Office in Oregon on charges of first-degree rape, first-degree unlawful sexual penetration and two counts of second-degree sexual abuse.{{Cite web |date=2024-04-10 |title=Former Portland Trail Blazers guard Ben McLemore arrested, accused of first-degree rape |url=https://www.kgw.com/article/news/crime/former-nba-player-ben-mclemore-arrested-accused-rape/283-e995665c-c2a1-4041-acea-d25715dbbf80 |access-date=2024-04-10 |website=kgw.com |language=en-US}} The charges stemmed from a party that took place at the home of then-Trail Blazers teammate [[Robert Covington]] in [[Lake Oswego]] on the night of October 3, 2021.{{Cite web |last=Bernstein |first=Maxine |date=June 25, 2025 |title=Ex-Trail Blazer Robert Covington testifies in former teammate's rape trial |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/galleries/KQVYT2CMYJH25FDAH4A32NC2QQ/ |website=oregonlive.com}} A 21-year-old woman at the party became incapacitated after a night of heavy drinking and awoke in the morning to McLemore raping her on a couch. The victim reported the crime to police on the same day of the incident.{{cite web |last1=Macuk |first1=Anthony |last2=Stevens |first2=Celine |title=Trial begins for former Trail Blazer Ben McLemore on rape charge |url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/crime/trial-begins-for-former-trail-blazer-ben-mclemore-on-rape-charge/ar-AA1GYLr0 |website=MSN.com |access-date=July 12, 2025 |date=June 17, 2025}} Police collected available evidence and the criminal investigation was assigned to detectives.{{cite web |title=Former Portland Trailblazer Charged With Sexual Assault |url=https://www.ci.oswego.or.us/police/former-portland-trailblazer-charged-sexual-assault |website=Arts Council of Lake Oswego |access-date=July 12, 2025 |date=April 10, 2024}} McLemore's departure from Oregon and his frequent overseas travel due to his career caused delays in the investigation. In February 2024, evidence was presented to a Clackamas County Grand Jury including testimony from the victim and an arrest warrant was subsequently issued for McLemore. On July 3, 2025, McLemore was found guilty of first-degree rape, first-degree unlawful sexual penetration and one count of second-degree sexual abuse by a jury after a 16-day trial.{{Cite web |first=Baxter |last=Holmes |date=2025-07-09 |title=Ben McLemore sentenced to 100 months in prison after rape conviction |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45703346 |website=ESPN.com |language=en|access-date=2026-08-30}} He was found not guilty of an additional count of second-degree sexual abuse.
